subject: Rollforward evidence & retention protocol for VM scans and CVE closure
messages:
From: Samir Malik <samir@brightline.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: evidence for VM scan cadence + closure rollforward and retention protocol

Hi Kimberly,

Quick ask from our SOC2 auditor: we need a compact evidence packet showing Redwood's current vulnerability management posture focused on three items for Brightline's assessment: 1) actual scan cadence and signed scan manifests (last 6 months), 2) CVE closure rollforward windows and canary/production rollout practices (how you ensure fixes propagate), and 3) evidence retention policy for scan artifacts / raw logs and signed attestations for closed CVEs (we need durable proofs for audit).

A couple of specifics that would speed review:
- Clear statement of SLA windows by severity (e.g., critical/active exploit, high, medium) and any escalation paths.
- A copy of the most recent scan manifest with hashes (we'd like an integrity chain).
- How you retain and compress artifacts (retention TTLs and where artifacts live).
- If you use a third-party escrow/hotfix witness, an indication of who that is and the witness process.

Can you send something by EOD next Wednesday (Aug 5)? If you prefer, send a short packet now and we'll follow-up with questions.

Thanks,
Samir Malik
Security Assurance Manager — Brightline Financial
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Samir Malik <samir@brightline.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for VM scan cadence + closure rollforward and retention protocol

Samir —

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching a compact packet to start (scan_manifest_20250728.pdf and evidence-retention-policy-2025.docx). High-level summary below; more granular artifacts and the signed manifest with hash chain will follow by Friday: 1) SLA windows and escalation: Critical (public exploit) — initial mitigation/patch within 48 hours, emergency canary + rollback safety; High — target remediation within 7 days; Medium/Low — scheduled based on risk window (30/90 days). We escalate Critical items to the on-call infra lead and notify customers via status if the exploit is customer-impacting. 2) Scan cadence: weekly authenticated network and container image scans, nightly CVE delta jobs for base images; monthly full application scans. Manifests include scan timestamp, tool/version, asset inventory snapshot, and content hashes. 3) Rollforward and rollout practice: we run a staged rollforward — dev -> canary (5%) -> regional progressive rollout -> full. Canary windows are minimum 24 hours under active monitoring; hotfixes can be pushed to 100% if the fix is verified and regression tests pass. 4) Retention: raw scan artifacts kept for 12 months in read-optimized storage, compressed manifests and signed evidence retained for 3 years; proof-of-closure index (CVE -> internal ticket id -> manifest hash) retained for 7 years. 5) Third-party witness: we maintain a contractual hotfix escrow arrangement with PatchWitness Inc.; they hold signed manifests for priority CVEs for 90 days post-closure as an independent witness.

Attachments: scan_manifest_20250728.pdf (compact manifest), evidence-retention-policy-2025.docx (policy summary). We'll upload raw artifacts and the larger CSV index to the shared Drive and send the DocuSign-ready signed manifest by Friday.

Let me know if you want us to map CVEs to your ticket IDs in the manifest before we sign.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security Compliance — Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, Samir Malik <samir@brightline.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for VM scan cadence + closure rollforward and retention protocol

Kimberly / Samir —

Adding a few operational details to complement Kimberly's summary and the initial packet:
- Patch rollforward schedule: for non-critical fixes we plan a 3-stage rollout over 7 days (canary 24h, regional 48-72h, global complete by day 7). For critical public exploit CVEs we shorten this to emergency canary (6-12h observation) then immediate progressive rollout within 48h.
- Monitoring gates: rollforward proceeds only if key metrics (latency, error rate, CPU) are within configured thresholds and automated synthetic checks pass. We keep immutable logs of gate checks with timestamps and IDs.
- Evidence index: we'll provide evidence-retention-index.csv (not attached here) mapping cve -> redwood-ticket-id -> manifest-hash -> retention-expiry. That index is signed and timestamped before export.
- Escrow witness process: PatchWitness Inc. receives the signed manifest and holds a notarized receipt; they will release their witness copy to auditors on request for 90 days.

I've attached the detailed schedule spreadsheet (patch_rollforward_schedule_20250730.xlsx) with canary windows and rollback criteria. No SLA exceptions currently in place for Brightline. If you need a formal attestation letter signed by our CISO for inclusion in your CAIQ/SIG packet, Laura can prepare that.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head, Vulnerability Response — Redwood Inference
From: Samir Malik <samir@brightline.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 02 Aug 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for VM scan cadence + closure rollforward and retention protocol

Kim / Karthik —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the packet so far. A couple quick follow-ups before we close the ticket: 1) Could you include a column in the evidence-retention-index mapping each CVE to our Brightline ticket ID (we will share the list as a CSV)? 2) For the signed manifest we need the manifest to include a simple CVE -> Redwood ticket -> PatchWitness receipt hash mapping so the auditor can verify chain-of-custody without pulling raw logs. 3) We'll accept the DocuSign attestation if Laura can include CISO signature and the region statement (US).

If you can push the updated index and the DocuSign-ready manifest by Monday EOD our auditor will be able to mark this as resolved for the SOC2 intake. Sending the acceptance link here: https://docusign.com/embedded/accept/BR-5492

Thanks — once we have the signed manifest we'll update the control evidence and close the item.

Samir Malik
Security Assurance Manager — Brightline Financial
